title: Meet the Fathers in 20 days
about: One Father a day: who they were, a passage they loved, and where to start reading them.

items.text: Bishop of Antioch after the Apostles. On his way to martyrdom in Rome he wrote seven letters on unity, the bishop and the Eucharist. Feast: 20 December.

items.father: St Ignatius of Antioch: Epistle to the Ephesians

items.text: A disciple of St John the Apostle and bishop of Smyrna, burned for Christ at 86. His letter and the account of his martyrdom are among the oldest Christian writings. Feast: 23 February.

items.father: St Polycarp of Smyrna: Epistle to the Philippians

items.text: A philosopher who found Christ and defended the faith before the emperors. His First Apology gives the oldest description of the Sunday Liturgy. Feast: 1 June.

items.father: St Justin Martyr: First Apology

items.text: A disciple of St Polycarp and bishop of Lyons. Against Heresies answers the Gnostics with the faith handed down from the Apostles. Feast: 23 August.

items.father: St Irenaeus of Lyons: Adversus haereses

items.text: Bishop of Carthage and martyr. He wrote on the unity of the Church, the Lord's Prayer and those who fell away in persecution. Feast: 31 August.

items.father: St Cyprian of Carthage: The Life and Passion of Cyprian

items.text: Bishop of Alexandria, exiled five times for defending the faith of Nicaea. On the Incarnation is one of the best books ever written on why God became man. Feast: 18 January, 2 May.

items.father: St Athanasius the Great: Against the Heathen

items.text: Archbishop of Caesarea, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs. He wrote On the Holy Spirit and gave the Church the Liturgy that bears his name. Feast: 1 January, 30 January.

items.father: St Basil the Great: De Spiritu Sancto

items.text: Archbishop of Constantinople, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs. His Theological Orations are the classic teaching on the Holy Trinity. Feast: 25 January, 30 January.

items.father: St Gregory the Theologian: Orations

items.text: Brother of St Basil and a great teacher on the Trinity, the soul and the endless growth of the soul toward God. Feast: 10 January.

items.father: St Gregory of Nyssa: Against Eunomius

items.text: Archbishop of Jerusalem. His Catechetical Lectures explain the Creed and the Holy Mysteries to the newly baptised. Feast: 18 March.

items.father: St Cyril of Jerusalem: Catechetical Lectures

items.text: Deacon of Nisibis and Edessa, the 'Harp of the Spirit'. His hymns teach the faith in poetry. His Lenten prayer is said in every Orthodox church. Feast: 28 January.

items.father: St Ephrem the Syrian: Nisibene Hymns

items.text: Archbishop of Constantinople and the Church's greatest preacher, one of the Three Holy Hierarchs. His homilies go verse by verse through much of the New Testament. The Divine Liturgy most often served bears his name. Feast: 13 November, 30 January.

items.father: St John Chrysostom: Homilies on the Gospel of St. Matthew

items.text: Bishop of Milan, who baptised Augustine and stood up to an emperor. A great preacher and hymn writer. Feast: 7 December.

items.father: St Ambrose of Milan: On the Christian Faith (De fide)

items.text: Priest, monk and Bible scholar who translated the Scriptures into Latin and lived his last years in Bethlehem. Feast: 15 June.

items.father: St Jerome: Letters

items.text: Bishop of Hippo in North Africa. His Confessions are loved by all Christians. The Orthodox honour him while setting aside parts of his teaching, such as his view of the Holy Spirit's procession and of grace. Feast: 15 June.

items.father: Blessed Augustine of Hippo: Confessions

items.text: A monk who learned from the Desert Fathers of Egypt and brought their teaching to the West in his Institutes and Conferences. Feast: 29 February (28 February).

items.father: St John Cassian: Institutes

items.text: Bishop of Rome. His Tome was read at the Council of Chalcedon on the two natures of Christ. Feast: 18 February.

items.father: St Leo the Great: Sermons

items.text: Bishop of Rome, a monk and pastor. The Orthodox call him the Dialogist after his Dialogues, and serve the Liturgy of the Presanctified Gifts in his name. Feast: 12 March.

items.father: St Gregory the Dialogist: Pastoral Rule

items.text: A monk of St Sabbas and great defender of the holy icons. His Exposition of the Orthodox Faith sums up the teaching of the Fathers before him. Feast: 4 December.

items.father: St John of Damascus: Exposition of the Faith

items.text: Bishop in Gaul, called the 'Athanasius of the West' for defending the faith of Nicaea. Feast: 13 January.

items.father: St Hilary of Poitiers: On the Councils, or the Faith of the Easterns
